Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres — Nxeon hosting platform), a real git repo. Standing rule: NEVER build/run dev servers/run `npm run build` in the live prod tree `/opt/nxeon` or the shared staging tree `/opt/nxeon-staging` — a past agent clobbering `.next` there broke production. Start by creating your own isolated worktree:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-visitors-ui -b feature/admin-visitors-ui-fixes
cd /opt/nxeon-wip-visitors-ui && npm install
```
Do ALL reading, editing, building, and testing inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-visitors-ui` from that point on.

GOAL: fix a batch of real UI/UX problems on the admin Visitor Analytics page (`/admin/visitors`), reported by the platform owner from live screenshots. The relevant files, already identified:
- `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` — composes everything: `ExcludeIpPanel` (the "Hidden IPs" section), `VisitorGlobe`, `RankedList`/`RecentVisitsTable`/`TrafficFeedTable` (all from `components/admin/VisitorStats.tsx`), `TrafficFeedFilter` (`components/admin/TrafficFeedFilter.tsx`, a separate date/kind/direction filter component), and pagination via `lib/pagination.ts`'s `paginate`/`pageHref`.
- `components/admin/ExcludeIpPanel.tsx` — the "Hidden IPs" chip list + add-IP input, currently rendered inline near the top of the page, always visible with every hidden IP shown as a chip.
- `components/admin/VisitorStats.tsx` — has both `RecentVisitsTable` and `TrafficFeedTable`.
- `components/admin/TrafficFeedFilter.tsx` — the date-range/kind/direction filter controls, currently a separate card above `TrafficFeedTable`.
- `components/admin/VisitorGlobe.tsx` — the live activity globe visualization.

Six concrete fixes requested, in the owner's own words:

1. **"Hide all of the hidden IPs, and have a clickable link/button to View Hidden IPs which brings up a popup of all of the IPs."** Currently `ExcludeIpPanel` shows every hidden IP as a chip inline, all the time (screenshot shows ~20 IP chips cluttering the page). Change it to show just a summary + a "View hidden IPs (N)" button that opens a modal/popup listing them (with the existing remove-IP "×" buttons and the add-IP input still functional inside that popup). Look for an existing modal/dialog pattern already used elsewhere in `components/admin/` to match this codebase's established style rather than inventing a new one.

2. **"Move the Hide IPs to the bottom of the page."** `ExcludeIpPanel` currently renders near the top of `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` (right after the page header). Move it to the bottom, after everything else.

3. **"Recent visits and Traffic Feed are literally the same thing, remove the Recent Visitors card."** Confirm this by reading both `RecentVisitsTable` and `TrafficFeedTable` in `VisitorStats.tsx` — if they are indeed duplicative (same data, same shape, just possibly different props/labels), remove `RecentVisitsTable` and its render call in `page.tsx` entirely, along with its now-unused query/data-fetch if nothing else uses it. If they actually serve genuinely different purposes on closer reading (e.g., different data windows or fields), don't blindly delete — note the discrepancy in your final report instead of guessing.

4. **Pagination is broken ("every time we click next page...")** — diagnose the actual bug in how `page.tsx` reads the page param and calls `paginate`/`pageHref` (`lib/pagination.ts`) for the traffic feed, and in how `TrafficFeedFilter` and `TrafficFeedTable` currently live as two separate cards. Fix pagination for real (test by actually clicking through multiple pages once verification is possible — see below) AND combine `TrafficFeedFilter` + `TrafficFeedTable` into ONE visual card/container instead of two separate ones.

5. **"Any time we set something [date/filter], it brings us to the top of the screen."** Changing a date-range/kind/direction filter currently causes a hard scroll-to-top — almost certainly because the filter change triggers a full navigation (`router.push`/`<Link>`/form submit to a new URL) that resets scroll position. Fix this so changing a filter doesn't jerk the viewport back to the top — e.g. `router.push(url, { scroll: false })` if using Next's router, or an equivalent fix appropriate to however `TrafficFeedFilter` currently triggers updates. Same scroll-preservation fix should apply to the pagination "next page" control from point 4, if it has the same issue.

6. **"Widen it up a bit because it gets slightly cut off."** The combined filter+feed card (post fix #4) is somewhat too narrow on the live page — check the actual rendered widths/container classes and widen appropriately (e.g. the date-range inputs or column headers being cut off at the current width) — use your judgment on the right width once you can see it rendered, per the visual verification step below.

7. **"Big open space below the globe animation card."** `VisitorGlobe.tsx` (or its container in `page.tsx`) apparently leaves a large empty gap beneath it — read the component and its container's layout (height/flex/grid classes) to find why, and fix the layout so there's no dead space. This might be caused by a fixed-height container that doesn't match the globe's actual rendered content height, or a sibling grid cell forcing extra height.

## Verification (required before reporting done)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full test suite (`npm test`), diffed by exact failing-test-name against a fresh run on `main` in the same worktree — zero NEW failures.
3. Visual verification is essential here since these are all layout/UX bugs — take Playwright screenshots of `/admin/visitors` at a normal desktop viewport (this page doesn't need to run in a full staging deploy; if you can get a local `npm run dev`/`next start` server running against a copy of the schema in your worktree pointed at a database, use that — otherwise, do your best with static analysis of the DOM structure and be explicit in your report about what you could and couldn't visually confirm). Confirm specifically: hidden-IPs list is collapsed behind a button by default and the popup opens correctly; Hide-IPs section is now at the bottom; only one "recent visits"-style table remains; clicking to page 2 of the traffic feed actually shows different/next rows; changing the date filter or paging does NOT scroll the viewport to the top; the traffic feed's combined card isn't visually cut off at its edges; there's no dead gap below the globe card.
4. Commit your work on the `feature/admin-visitors-ui-fixes` branch inside the worktree (do not push, do not merge to main, do not deploy anywhere).

Report back with: what you found for each of the 7 items above (especially whether Recent Visits vs Traffic Feed really are duplicates), the exact files changed, confirmation of tsc/test results, what you could/couldn't visually verify and how, and anything you deliberately left as a judgment call (e.g. exact modal styling, exact widened pixel/rem value) since those are product/UX calls, not technical blockers.

The odd part is that the first click on "Next" didn't change the URL or content, but clicking it a second time (against a freshly re-rendered locator) actually navigated to page 2. That suggests either the first click was intercepted or absorbed by something without triggering navigation, or there's a timing issue where my `networkidle` wait resolved before the client-side transition's fetch actually completed, making it look like the first click failed when it just hadn't finished yet.

If the RSC transition takes a second or two due to those parallel DB queries, and the button gives zero loading feedback, an impatient user clicking twice could interrupt the first navigation with a second one. While building a modal for /opt/nxeon's admin Visitor Analytics page (app/admin/layout.tsx wraps every admin page's content in `<main>`), I found that `<main>` carries `animate-fade-up` (defined in app/globals.css: `@keyframes fade-up { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }`, applied as `animation: fade-up 0.4s ease-out both`). Because the fill-mode is `both`, the "to" keyframe's `transform: translateY(0)` (computed as `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`, an identity transform) persists on `<main>` FOREVER after the 0.4s animation finishes — not just during it.

Per the CSS spec, ANY non-none `transform` on an ancestor — even a no-op identity transform — creates a new containing block for descendant `position: fixed` elements, making them position relative to that ancestor's box instead of the viewport. This means every `position: fixed` modal/dialog anywhere under `<main>` in the entire admin panel (e.g. components/admin/BoardClient.tsx's AppSettingsModal and CardModal, both using `className="fixed inset-0 ..."`, and any new ones) does NOT actually stay pinned to the visible viewport — it renders positioned relative to `<main>`'s box, which visually means the popup can appear scrolled far off-screen (e.g. below the fold) instead of centered over whatever the admin is currently looking at, especially on long pages. I verified this concretely with Playwright: opened a `fixed inset-0` modal near the bottom of a long admin page and its `getBoundingClientRect()` came out at document-relative coordinates (top ~848px while `window.scrollY` was 1797 and viewport height was 1000px) instead of viewport-relative ones, and confirmed the offending ancestor via computed style walk — `<main class="mx-auto w-full max-w-7xl flex-1 px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 animate-fade-up">` has `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`.

Fix options to evaluate: (a) stop applying the fade-up transform-based animation directly to `<main>` — move it to an inner wrapper div instead so `<main>` itself never gets a `transform`, or (b) change the animation to animate only `opacity` (no `transform`) so there's nothing to leave a lingering non-none transform, or (c) add an `onAnimationEnd` handler that resets `main.style.transform = ""` once the intro animation finishes. Whichever approach, verify afterward with a real modal (BoardClient's AppSettingsModal is a convenient one to test against) that `position: fixed` elements under `<main>` are truly viewport-relative regardless of scroll position — check `getBoundingClientRect()` stays independent of `window.scrollY`. This is sitewide (affects every admin page since app/admin/layout.tsx is shared), so a single targeted fix to the animation/wrapper should resolve it everywhere at once. Not urgent/user-facing-breaking (modals still function, just mispositioned), but worth fixing since it silently breaks every popup in the admin surface.
